sections.body_md:
Rank counts independent directions in a matrix. The null space is every vector the matrix sends to zero. The determinant of a square matrix is zero exactly when that null space contains a nonzero vector. A matrix-vector product is the mixture of the columns given by the entries of the vector.

For any matrix, rank plus the dimension of the null space equals the number of columns. A row that is a copy of another row does not raise the rank. Elimination makes the count visible: the number of nonzero rows that remain is the rank. None of this depends on a particular plant. Eigenvalues, and a change of basis that diagonalizes a matrix, are the next skill.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md: For \(A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}\), \[ \det A = ad - bc. \] Rank plus nullity equals the number of columns. The product \(Av\) is a linear combination of the columns of \(A\), with weights taken from \(v\). A square matrix has a nonzero null vector exactly when its determinant is zero.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
Take \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\). The second column is three times the first, so the rank is 1 and the determinant is 0. A null vector is \(\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}\), because \(B\) sends it to zero.

Separately, \(C\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix}\) with \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\) gives \(x = 1\), \(y = 2\): from \(5x + y = 7\) and \(2x + 3y = 8\), elimination produces \(13y = 26\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Calling a matrix full rank because no entry is zero. Every entry can be nonzero while the rank is 1.
- Confusing the column space, which is everything the matrix can produce, with the null space, which is everything the matrix sends to zero.
- Adding the diagonal products instead of subtracting them in a 2 by 2 determinant.
- Counting rows, rather than independent columns, as the rank of a tall matrix.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Reachability stacks input directions and asks whether the rank equals the number of states. Observability stacks output directions and asks the same question. Least squares needs the columns of the data matrix to be independent before the normal equations have one solution. Eigenvalues are the stretch factors of a square matrix, and they are a separate skill.
